title: Patient Financial Account Terms — Late Fees Joined to a Returned-Payment Replacement
content:
**Term.** Late fees join a returned-payment replacement on the Patient Financial Account according to the return history:

- when the account has at least the tier's number of returned payments before restriction — 2 on every financial class — of returned check or ACH payments in the 12 calendar months before the handling date, and late fees were posted in those 12 months, every such late fee is included;
- when it has fewer returned check or ACH payments, and late fees were posted in those 12 months, only the most recent late fee is included;
- when no late fee was posted in those 12 months, none is included.

**Terms explained.** A returned check or ACH payment is a payment reversal on the ledger whose method was check or ACH, counted by the reversal date. A late fee is a charge with the line category late fee, counted by its posting date. A window of calendar months for the returned-payment replacement ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it.

| Check or ACH returns in the 12 months | Late fees posted in the 12 months | Late fees included |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | one or more | every late fee of the 12 months |
| 0 or 1 | one or more | the most recent late fee only |
| any | none | none |

**Hypothetical example.** Late fees of 10.00 were posted in February and in June, both inside the 12 months. With two returns in the 12 months, 20.00 of late fees is included; with one return, only the June fee of 10.00 is included; had both fees been posted more than 12 months before the handling date, none would be included.
